pairs.question: Dic ubi sit, germane, parens; stat summa caputque orbis, an occidimus Romanaque Magnus ad umbras abstulit?
pairs.answer: Non Caesaris armis occubuit dignoque perit auctore ruinae: rege sub inpuro Nilotica rura tenente, hospitii fretus superis et munere tanto in proauos, cecidit donati uictima regni.
pairs.derivation: Sextus asks his brother Gnaeus where their father Pompey is and whether he still stands or has perished. Question is the full direct utterance; stripped the trailing speech-tag 'haec fatur; quem contra talia frater:'. For the answer, skipped the brother's non-answering apostrophe preamble 'o felix, quem sors alias dispersit in oras / quique nefas audis: oculos, germane, nocentis / spectato genitore fero.' and began at the operative answering sentence 'non Caesaris armis...', which states how and where Magnus died (slain under the foul Egyptian king as victim of the kingdom he had given). Ended at 'donati uictima regni.' (first full stop), where the brother turns from answering to recounting what he himself witnessed ('uidi ego magnanimi lacerantes pectora patris...').
